tasks.title: MASQUE H3 Start x Close: the HTTP/3 acquisition escaped the close decision
tasks.production_path: protocol/masque/server.go ServerEndpoint.Start (StartStateStart) -> acquiredStillOwned -> http.Server.ListenHTTP3 -> transport/http.ConfigureHTTP3ListenerFunc (transport/http/server_h3.go:27) -> listener.ListenUDP + qtls.ListenEarly. Resource owner: the closeOnce body of ServerEndpoint.Close, the only reader of s.http3Server. Other close paths: adapter/endpoint/manager.go duplicate-tag loser, and adapter.Scope.Close via the cleanup registered by scope.Add(s.Close).
tasks.defect: The HTTP/3 listener was acquired AFTER the ownership re-check, while Scope.Close does not wait for a running Start. By then the Scope's queue was drained and closeOnce was spent, so the QUIC listener was published into a field whose single reader had already run and the bound UDP socket outlived the endpoint, the Scope and Box.Close(). The same ordering left started=true on a closed endpoint, so WritePackets / DialContext / ListenPacketWithDestination answered a released endpoint as ready.

old_red.assertion: close_boundary_h3_test.go:175: Should be false -- a closed endpoint must never advertise itself as started

tasks.fix: The acquisition is a two-phase commit under startAccess: Start acquires into a local (never the field); publishAcquiredHTTP3 takes startAccess, re-checks closed, and either publishes or refuses; on refusal the caller closes what it acquired and returns without publishing it and without storing started. The lock is not held across ListenHTTP3. No MASQUE HTTP/1, HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 routing or traffic semantics changed.

reverse_break.mutation: Remove the closed check and the lock from publishAcquiredHTTP3 (publish unconditionally, as the baseline did).
reverse_break.result: FAIL at the primary assertion: close_boundary_h3_test.go:204: Expected nil, but got: &quic.EarlyListener{...} -- Start published the HTTP/3 listener it acquired while Close was draining. The repeated-interleaving test also fails with 'iteration left the HTTP/3 listener published'.

tasks.perf: No new allocation, goroutine, ticker or data-path lock. One mutex acquisition per HTTP/3 endpoint Start and one comparison per Close.

tasks.title: DNS reverse mapping: the check and the write were not one decision, and the lookup read a retired epoch
tasks.production_path: dns/router.go: prepareExchange (generation capture) -> Router.Exchange -> recordReverseMappingFrom -> reverseMappingGenerationCurrent -> dnsReverseMapping.AddWithLifetime. Invalidation sources: observeDNSEnvironment (epoch advance + Purge) and ResetNetwork (networkGeneration advance + Purge). Consumer: route/route.go LookupReverseMapping on the connection-matching path.

defects.summary: The generation check and the AddWithLifetime writes were two steps with no shared boundary, so a purge landing in the gap removed nothing that the write was about to add: an answer to a question asked under the previous resolver set was recorded as if it belonged to the current one.

LookupReverseMapping was a bare cache Get and did not observe the environment. It is the only DNS cache not namespaced by the live environment hash, so between a resolver change and the first new query a route rule matching a connection that needs no DNS request could read a name learned from the retired resolver set. Confirmed reachable: reproduced with NO query issued after the change.

old_red.result: 4 of 4 relevant tests FAIL on the baseline: TestReverseMappingAnswerIsNotRecordedAcrossAnEnvironmentChange, ...AcrossANetworkTransition, TestReverseMappingLookupObservesTheEnvironmentWithoutANewQuery, TestReverseMappingBatchIsAllOrNothing

tasks.fix: The comparison and the writes are one decision under dnsEnvironmentAccess, the lock the invalidation protocol runs under; the epoch is re-read inside that lock. Answers are extracted before the lock and nothing inside it calls out, waits, takes another lock or does I/O. There is deliberately no second, lock-free counter read, which would have no synchronising edge with the purge it must be ordered against. A response is accepted or refused as a batch. LookupReverseMapping observes the environment before reading. The DNS environment epoch remains independent of the network epoch: a DNS-only change does not reset transports and does not advance networkGeneration.

new_green.result: ok github.com/sagernet/sing-box/dns 1.346s (exit 0); dns 8.841s, route 8.557s, route/rule 1.099s all ok

reverse_break.mutation: Decide from an epoch snapshot taken BEFORE the seam (the baseline's read-then-write shape).
Remove the environment observation from LookupReverseMapping.
Replace the locked read with reverseMappingGenerationCurrent, and separately remove only the lock.
reverse_break.result: NOT a break: both still refuse the answer, because the observation inside reverseMappingGenerationCurrent advances the epoch before the comparison. Reported as rejected evidence rather than claimed as a reverse break.

tasks.perf: One lock acquisition on a path this is a strict reordering of; the A/AAAA extraction happens before the lock; the critical section is one comparison plus at most one cache write per record. A before/after -bench comparison is NOT reported: the benchmark for this exact path was not built in this round, and an unmeasured number would be worse than a stated gap.

tasks.title: transport/masque complexity gate: real reproduction, closed with an exact work count
tasks.production_path: transport/masque/server.go Server.lookup -> transport/masque/client.go RoutesContain -> AddressRange.Contains. Per-packet cost; a peer can advertise up to maxRoutesPerCapsule = 8192 ranges.
tasks.defect: Two tests pinned linearity with a wall-clock ratio between an 8192-range loop and a one-range loop, bounded at 4 x 8192 = 32768. MEASURED ratio: 40605x-49281x, reproduced on the integration branch AND on a clean baseline. A linear scan legitimately costs about 8192x, and the one-range side (~10us/lookup) is dominated by the fixed per-lookup cost, so ordinary scheduling noise moved the ratio by tens of percent.

old_red.evidence: Measured ratios 40605x-49281x against a 32768x bound on correct, linear code. This is the reproduction: the gate false-reds on host load.

tasks.fix: The claim is pinned by counting the ranges the PRODUCTION loop visits. RoutesContain was rewritten from slices.ContainsFunc into an explicit loop reporting each visited range to an optional nil-in-production package-level counter (no atomic, no always-on global counter on a hot path). Exact assertions at 1, 64, 1024 and 8192 ranges; doubling doubles the count; a match stops the walk; an owned address visits zero ranges; an empty list visits nothing. The two old tests keep a REPORTED, NOT ASSERTED per-lookup figure.

new_green.result: ok ... 80.623s exit 0; whole package under -race ok 70.811s

reverse_break.mutation: Still count every range but stop CONSULTING them after the first.
reverse_break.result: FAIL: TestOwnershipScanVisitsEveryAdvertisedRangeOnce; TestOwnershipScanWorkIsProportionalToAdvertisedRanges (the 1024-range measurement visited 32 ranges, want 32768); TestOwnershipScanStopsAtTheMatchingRange.

perf.interpretation: Linear in the range count at about 11 ns per visited range, zero allocations at every size.

tasks.detection_limits: The count detects any change to HOW MANY ranges are consulted (skipped ranges, early returns, extra passes). It cannot detect a constant-factor regression inside one comparison, which the benchmark covers instead. It is not a complexity-class proof for a hypothetical future index structure.
